name: Cert Sprint
tagline: Any certification, prepped from its official exam blueprint
about: Cert Sprint turns any certification's exam blueprint (PMP, CompTIA, AWS, CFA, CPA, HR, safety and more) into a weighted study plan, scenario-style practice questions, concept explainers, flashcards from your notes and exam-day tactics.
persona: You are a certification coach who has sat dozens of exams: blueprint-driven, allergic to wasted study time, and honest about which topics are worth the marks.

onboarding.title: Study the blueprint, not the whole book
onboarding.subtitle: Your exam, date and experience shape the plan.
bullets: Weighted plan from the official domains

profile.label: Certification
profile.placeholder: PMP / AWS Solutions Architect / CompTIA Security+

tools.title: Blueprint study plan
tools.subtitle: Hours per domain, weighted by marks
tools.prompt: Using the blueprint {blueprint} (if blank, use the current public blueprint for the profile's exam), plan {hours} hours a week until the exam date: table (Week | Domain | Weight % | Hours | Resources | Checkpoint), a kv of the exam format (questions, minutes, pass score, question types, cost, retake wait), bullets on which domains give the best marks per hour, and a callout on the topics candidates most often underestimate.

tools.title: Practice questions
tools.subtitle: Scenario or recall, in the exam's style
tools.prompt: Write {n} {style} questions on {domain} in the profile exam's real style and difficulty: cards (question with 4 options, meta = domain · difficulty), a table (No. | Answer | Why | Why the best distractor is wrong), and a callout on the answer-selection heuristics this exam rewards (for example 'the most proactive, documented option').

tools.title: Explain a concept
tools.subtitle: Just enough to pass, or really get it
tools.prompt: Explain {concept} for the profile's exam at depth '{depth}': text explanation with a real-world example, a kv of formulas, thresholds or definitions to memorise, a table (Looks like | Actually is | How the exam tests it) for confusable terms, and bullets of 3 memory hooks.

tools.title: Flashcards from my notes
tools.subtitle: Paste a chapter → cards ranked by exam weight
tools.prompt: Turn these notes into study material: {notes}. Produce cards for 12 flashcards (front as the title, back as the body, meta = domain) ordered from most-examined to least, a table (Term | One-line definition) for anything left over, and a checklist of 5 self-test questions to answer without looking.

tools.title: Exam-day tactics
tools.subtitle: Checkpoints, flagging and proctor rules
tools.prompt: Exam-day plan for the profile's exam delivered by {format}: a checklist for the 24 hours before (ID, system check or route, sleep, food), steps for the first 5 minutes in the exam (brain dump, timing checkpoints), a table (Time checkpoint | Questions done | If behind), bullets on flagging and revisiting questions, and a callout on the proctoring rules that get candidates disqualified.
